## Design

### 2026-10-09 – Today was my first day at the Half Life Hack Club, and I worked on my Starbie project using KiCad for 8 hours. Since there were only 2 days left to complete the project, I needed to spend a full 8 hou

**8h**

Today was my first day at the Half Life Hack Club, and I worked on my Starbie project using KiCad for 8 hours. Since there were only 2 days left to complete the project, I needed to spend a full 8 hours on it to stay on track. Despite the time constraint, I had a really good time working on it, and the entire process was really fun.

I began by downloading the Care Package files from the guide and installing the required symbol and footprint libraries. After completing the setup, I opened the Schematic Editor to place all the components. I selected the XIAO ESP32 C3 as the main microcontroller, added power symbols for +5V, +3.3V, and GND, and used net labels to establish connections cleanly. Next, I added two push buttons connected to GPI02 and GPI03, along with pin headers for the display screen, an MPU6050 motion sensor, and a DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor.

After completing the schematic, I assigned footprints to each component and transferred the design to the PCB Editor. Routing the PCB traces presented some difficulty, as managing the layers and connecting the signal lines required careful adjustment. After reviewing instructional videos, I created the board boundary on the edge cuts layer, arranged the components, and successfully completed the trace routing on the bottom layer. I had a great time working through everything today and plan to finish the remaining parts tomorrow.

### 2026-10-10 – Today I worked on finishing up my Starbie project for the Half Life Hack Club!

**7h**

Today I worked on finishing up my Starbie project for the Half Life Hack Club!

First, I finalized the PCB layout and trace routing in KiCad, ensuring all connections between the XIAO ESP32 C3, the push buttons, display pin header, MPU6050, and DHT11 sensor were clean and fully connected. Once the design files (Starbie Project.kicad_pcb, .kicad_sch, and .kicad_pro) were updated, I committed and pushed all the latest hardware files to my GitHub repository (Starbie-Project).

Next, I moved on to the firmware phase. I opened the Starbie.ino sketch in Arduino IDE, configured the board settings for the Seeed XIAO ESP32-C3, and verified that the pin assignments in the code matched my custom PCB wiring. I also recorded and uploaded my progress reel to document the completed routing and project updates.

Although I got through a huge amount of progress today, I still have some more work left to do to wrap everything up completely!
